blocks.text: Meeting Minutes: {{fact:f:E-2018-001.client}} Investor Relations Program
Working session with the client. Minutes taken by Michelle Black.
We left the session with the investor presentation one round from final and a plan for handing the program over to the team at {{fact:f:E-2018-001.client}}.
Present

items: Michael Morris, Partner, Ashcombe Advisory Partners
Laura Bradley, Senior Associate, Ashcombe Advisory Partners
Michelle Black, Communications Analyst, Ashcombe Advisory Partners

blocks.text: What we talked about

We began with the investor presentation. Lauren Heath had read the latest draft closely, and most of her comments were small wording points. Two went further. She wants the operating section to open with the measures the company's board already reviews, so investors and directors see the same figures in the same order. She also wants the outlook slide cut back to what the company has already said in public. We agreed with both. Laura Bradley will make the changes and send the revised draft with a clear version label, so everyone knows which file is up for approval.

I then took the group through the peer comparison. The headline is that most of the peer group says less about margins than our draft does, and more about customer retention. The figures come from the peers' own investor presentations and annual reports. In two places I had to rely on press coverage instead, and I said so. Michael Morris asked that we treat those two figures as unconfirmed until I have checked them against the companies' own documents. Until then they stay off the slides.

Next we turned to the investor Q&A. This is the document management will lean on once we step back, so it has to read the way they actually speak in a meeting. Lauren asked for fewer questions and shorter answers. We agreed to keep only the questions investors have raised during the program, plus a short section on the outlook that matches the trimmed slide. Laura will send it together with the presentation, with a cover note setting out exactly what each approval covers.

Most of the second half of the session was about handover. We are in the later part of the program, and Lauren was clear that she wants her own people running the investor calendar well before we finish. Michael suggested a short operating guide for the function. It would cover who watches the investor inbox, how meeting requests are logged, how drafts move through approval, and which materials get refreshed and when. Lauren liked the idea and asked us to keep it practical and brief. She will name the person on her team who will own it.

We also talked about the weekly coverage summary I send out. Lauren's team finds it useful and would like to keep it going after we leave. I will keep sending it for now. Before we finish, I will walk her team through how it is put together, including where each item comes from, so they can produce it themselves.
Who is doing what

Check the two press-sourced peer figures against the companies' own documents
Cut the investor Q&A to the questions raised in the program, plus an outlook section
Outline the investor relations operating guide
Name the owner of the investor calendar and inbox
Walk the client team through how the weekly coverage summary is built

blocks.text: Our next step is Laura's revised presentation. Once it is out, we will open the next session with Lauren's sign-off on it and take the rest from there.
Status Report: Investor Relations Program for {{fact:f:E-2018-001.client}}
Prepared by Michael Morris, Partner, for the leadership team at {{fact:f:E-2018-001.client}}, with input from Laura Bradley, Michelle Black and Sandra Mcdonald.
Where the program stands

We are now in the final weeks of the program, and almost everything we set out to build is finished and in your team's hands: the investor presentation and the investor Q&A have both been approved, the peer comparison has been checked line by line against its sources, and the operating guide for the investor relations function has gone to your team in draft. What remains is the handover itself, which means one last revision of the guide once your team has had a chance to work from it, a single joint call to transfer the investor calendar and the open meeting requests, and the close-out of our files at the end of the engagement.
Completed since our last report
Most of what follows was settled at the working sessions over the winter, and I have noted who carried each piece, because the people who did the work should get the credit for it.

Complete; one figure confirmed, one corrected

Investor meeting log and calendar set up in the format your team asked for, with the past meeting records transferred

blocks.text: What is left before we close

Three pieces of work remain, and none of them is large, but each one depends on a little time from your side: (1) a final revision of the operating guide, which Laura Bradley will make as soon as your team's comments come back, so that the version you keep reflects how your people actually handle investor requests; (2) a single handover call, which Sandra Mcdonald will organize with the owner your team named for the investor calendar, to walk through the calendar, the open meeting requests and the inbox rules so that nothing is left in flight on our side when we step back; and (3) the close-out of the engagement, in which we archive the working files, send you a clean set of the final approved materials, and issue our final invoice.
Risks

The main risk at this point is continuity. The operating guide only works if the person your team named to own the investor calendar has the time to keep it up, and if that job ends up spread across several people, the inbox and the meeting log will drift apart within a few months, which is exactly the problem the guide was written to prevent; we recommend that the owner sit in on the handover call and that one person, and only one, keeps the log.

Two smaller points are worth recording. The peer comparison reflects what the peer group had published as of this report, so it will start to age as soon as those companies next report, and it should be refreshed before it is used in any investor meeting later in the year. The approved outlook wording also needs care, because the slide and the matching section of the Q&A were approved as a pair, and any change to one should go back through the same approval route as the other before either is used.
Budget

The engagement budget is {{fact:f:E-2018-001.fee}}, as set out in the engagement letter, and we expect to finish within it; the remaining work is handover and close-out, both of which were part of the original scope, and we have not done, and do not expect to do, any work outside that scope that would call for a separate conversation about fees.
What we need from you

Since the last items on our list wait on your team, and we would like to close the program cleanly, we need your team's comments on the draft operating guide back to Laura Bradley within the coming week, and we need a time for the handover call that suits the owner of the investor calendar, which Sandra Mcdonald will put on the calendar as soon as you send one through.

Laura, Michelle, Sandra and I have valued working with your team over these months, and if anything in this report does not match your own view of where things stand, call me directly and we will settle it before the program closes.
